# en-formal

## Good example

Summary of Policy GP-07/2026: Gifts and Hospitality from Suppliers

Sample Port Authority, Compliance Office

The Board adopted Policy GP-07/2026 on 14 September 2026, after the 2025 internal review found 37 supplier gifts that appeared in no register. The policy replaces GP-03/2019 from 1 January 2027. This summary does not alter its terms, and where the two differ, the policy prevails.

Staff who take part in a tender may accept nothing from any bidder from the date the tender is advertised until 30 days after the contract is signed. Outside those periods, a member of staff may accept a gift worth up to $25, provided that the supplier has given that person no other gift in the same calendar year. Cash and vouchers must be refused at any value.

Every gift offered must be entered in the Gifts Register within 5 working days, including a gift that was refused. The Compliance Office reads the Register each quarter and reports to the Audit Committee any supplier named more than three times.

## Pair 1

### Before

In today's evolving governance landscape, Delegation of Authority allows an officer to exercise decision-making powers formally assigned to them by a more senior authority. In procurement, this allows approvals to be made at different levels within the organization, provided each delegate has the authority to act and follows the rules that apply to that authority.

It should be noted that delegation does not transfer responsibility. Moreover, a delegate remains accountable for every decision made under the delegated authority, and must be able to show that the decision was properly made. Furthermore, staff should therefore understand the limits of any delegation they hold before exercising it.

One of the most important limits concerns Conflicts of Interest. Section 12(3) of the Sample Housing Agency Procurement Regulation 2026 states: "A delegate shall not approve a purchase in which the delegate has a Conflict of Interest." A delegation therefore cannot be used to approve a purchase in which the delegate has a personal, financial, or other interest that may compromise their judgment.

[cut]

### After

One of the most important limits concerns Conflicts of Interest. ## Pair 2

### Before

FORMAL POLICY NOTICE

Declaration of Conflicts of Interest for Procurement Staff

Purpose

It is important to note that this notice sets out a mandatory requirement for the making of a declaration of any Conflict of Interest by all staff involved in procurement activities. The requirement is intended not only to protect the integrity of the procurement process but also to safeguard the organization's reputation and to ensure that decisions are made fairly and impartially.

Scope

This requirement applies to every member of staff who takes part in any stage of a procurement process, including the preparation of requirements, the evaluation of bids, the negotiation of contracts, and the management of suppliers.

Requirement

Furthermore, any staff member who identifies a Conflict of Interest must make a declaration of it in writing. Moreover, declarations must be submitted to Internal Audit within 3 working days of the conflict becoming known to the staff member.

Effective Date

This requirement takes effect on 1 December 2026.

Consequences of Non-Compliance

[cut]

### After

FORMAL POLICY NOTICE

Declaration of Conflicts of Interest for Procurement Staff

Purpose

This notice requires all staff involved in procurement activities to declare any Conflict of Interest. The requirement is intended to protect the integrity of the procurement process, to safeguard the organization's reputation, and to ensure that decisions are made fairly and impartially.

Scope

This requirement applies to every member of staff who takes part in any stage of a procurement process, including preparing requirements, evaluating bids, negotiating contracts, and managing suppliers.

Requirement

Any staff member who identifies a Conflict of Interest must declare it in writing. Declarations must be submitted to Internal Audit within 3 working days of the conflict becoming known to the staff member.

Effective Date

This requirement takes effect on 1 December 2026.

Consequences of Non-Compliance

Failure to declare a Conflict of Interest may result in disciplinary action in accordance with the applicable policies of the organization. Staff members who are uncertain whether a particular interest constitutes a conflict are encouraged to seek guidance from Internal Audit before taking any further action.

Enquiries

[cut]
